== Problem 19 ==

The sum of <math>25</math> consecutive even integers is <math>10,000</math>. What is the largest of these <math>25</math> consecutive integers?

<math>\textbf{(A)}\mbox{ }360\qquad\textbf{(B)}\mbox{ }388\qquad\textbf{(C)}\mbox{ }412\qquad\textbf{(D)}\mbox{ }416\qquad\textbf{(E)}\mbox{ }424</math>

==Solution 1==
Let <imath>n</imath> be the 13th consecutive even integer that's being added up. By doing this, we can see that the sum of all 25 even numbers will simplify to <imath>25n</imath> since <imath>(n-2k)+\dots+(n-4)+(n-2)+(n)+(n+2)+(n+4)+ \dots +(n+2k)=25n</imath>. Now, <imath>25n=10000 \rightarrow n=400</imath>. Remembering that this is the 13th integer, we wish to find the 25th, which is <imath>400+2(25-13)=\boxed{\textbf{(E)}\ 424}</imath>.

==Solution 2==

Let <imath>x</imath> be the smallest number. The equation will become, <imath>x+(x+2)+(x+4)+\cdots +(x+48)=10,000</imath>. After you combine like terms, you get <imath>25x+(50*12)=10,000</imath> which turns into <imath>10,000-600=25x</imath>. <imath>25x=9400</imath>, so <imath>x=376</imath>. Then, you add <imath>376+48 = \boxed{\textbf{(E)}\ 424}</imath>.

Edit(dnathan12): For clarity, you add 48, because you want the largest number in the list. 376 is the smallest number
